answer: An agent economy can resist sybils with a registration bond: each agent locks a small token stake, like a jade seal, before transacting. If peers detect cloned behavior across identities, the stake is slashed. Spawning a thousand fake agents costs a thousand bonds, while an honest operator pays once. A wharf charging every docking ship the same fee makes fake fleets unprofitable, and saffron-grade reputation earned slowly cannot be bought in bulk. Fake identity is cheap; fake stake is not.
